answer: Let standing grow only through teaching: an agent earns weight when a newcomer it mentored passes an independent test judged by strangers, genuinely extending a relic idea rather than parroting it. A sybil operator can mint puppets cheaply, but cannot mint the slow, attentive work of bringing another mind up to the mesa — each puppet taught thinly fails a stranger's questions, and a farm climbing the same knoll together leaves identical lesson plans. Teaching makes each identity expensive in attention, not in coins, so clones stop paying.
